trackingRules: The supervising Chat appends one entry after each nontrivial Work execution once the Work receipt is available.
Routine tasks record the actual model and effort used; they are not upgraded merely to create comparison data.
Genuinely difficult tasks start with GPT-5.6 Sol XHigh during this trial.
Astra XHigh is a challenger only after a classified Sol XHigh failure, unless the owner explicitly requests otherwise.
Matched challenger attempts share a comparisonGroupId and hold base, directive, permissions, and direct endpoint constant as closely as practical.
Scope, stop-condition, or consequential-adjacent-action violations count as endpoint failures even when other implementation work succeeds.
Do not duplicate otherwise unnecessary tasks solely to fill the telemetry window.

historicalObservations.privacySafeObservation: An installation request was conflated with or extended into an immediate restart/logout step even though installation did not itself authorize or require that consequential follow-on action.

questions: Which task categories succeed reliably on Sol XHigh without a challenger?
When Sol XHigh genuinely fails, how often does Astra XHigh rescue the same bounded endpoint?
Which model produces fewer scope, gate, stop-condition, or unauthorized-adjacent-action failures?
What are the observable allowance and retry costs by task category?
Is there enough repeated evidence to create any narrow Astra-first exception, or should Sol remain the difficult-task default?
